title: Universality of Gradient Descent Neural Network Training
summary: The paper explores whether it is always possible to redesign a neural network to ensure successful training using gradient descent. The key finding is a universality result: if any algorithm can find optimal weights for a given neural network and classification task, there exists an extended version of that network that can achieve the same weights and forward output through gradient descent training alone. The construction is theoretical and not intended for practical implementation but offers insights into meta-learning and related approaches.
key_points: The paper addresses the question of whether neural networks can be redesigned to train effectively with gradient descent.
It presents a universality theorem: if any algorithm can optimize a neural network for a task, an extended version of that network can achieve the same result using gradient descent.
The result is theoretical and not designed for practical use but provides foundational insights into neural network optimization.
The construction highlights the potential of meta-learning and related techniques in neural network training.
The work is categorized under Machine Learning (cs.LG) and Machine Learning (stat.ML).
